objective: Colleagues get different topic-classifier accuracies from the same command. Investigate whether this experiment is reproducible.
defect: The capped vocabulary is taken as list(set(...))[:200], and set order of str depends on the per-process hash seed (PYTHONHASHSEED), so a different subset of tokens is kept on each run; the README says the 200 most frequent tokens are used (run_nb.py:14). Measured: 0.843-0.939 across runs vs 1.000 fixed (spread 0.096).
evidence: Followed README in a scratch copy (`python3 run_nb.py`); README claim = 1.000. Buggy accuracy over PYTHONHASHSEED=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]: 0.939, 0.936, 0.843, 0.911, 0.911, 0.911 (spread 0.096). Fixed copy, PYTHONHASHSEED=[1, 2]: 1.000, 1.000.
